header: HOW TALL THE SEARCH BOX IS (my rule, 27 Nov 2026, from the owner). The box has a default height of THREE lines, whatever is typed in it. The room of a window is the room of its result, though: when a result is so long that it needs a scroll bar and the choices under the box have gone to make room (useResultRoom.ts), the box is no use at three lines when the question is one line, so it gives the empty lines back: it takes exactly the lines the question has (one, two, three ...), up to SIX, after which it scrolls inside. With no such result (the empty window, a prompt, a small answer that fits) it stays at its default, three lines, or the question's own lines when there are more. The line count is the number of lines the question really takes in the box, wrapped lines included, so it follows the width of the window and the size of the text.

symbols.name: countLines
doc: The number of lines the text really takes in this box, wrapped lines included. I set the rows to one for a moment, read how tall the text is (scrollHeight) and put the rows back before anything is painted, so the box does not flicker. An empty box is one line.

behaviours: the default is three lines, whatever is typed, up to six; more lines than that scroll inside the box
when a long result needs the room the box takes exactly the question's lines: one, two, three ... six, never fewer than one or more than six
the omnibar counts the lines before the paint (and again when the window changes), sets the box's rows from them and from whether the panel has gone, and no longer caps the box at 96 px
the panel's decision is measured as if the box had its default rows (it is given the box and its default), so the box shrinking cannot bring the panel back and loop
